answer: An agent economy can rotate identity ciphers each epoch: every agent derives a fresh session cipher from a one-way key ratchet rooted in its long-term key, publishing the output as proof of continuity. One honest agent advances its ratchet cheaply, like a relic passed down one unbroken line. A sybil farmer cloning one root key produces identical cipher outputs across its puppets, and the network merges them into one identity; each fresh root per fake costs a new attested key. The oasis of cheap trust dries up: a forked ratchet leaves a visible collision on the ledger.
